arxiv-2202-07773.title: The efficacy and generalizability of conditional GANs for posterior inference in physics-based inverse problems
arxiv-2202-07773.creator: Deep Ray, Harisankar Ramaswamy, Dhruv V. Patel, Assad A. Oberai
arxiv-2202-07773.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Deep Ray, Harisankar Ramaswamy, Dhruv V. Patel, Assad A. Oberai. In this work, we train conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial networks to effectively sample from the posterior of physics-based Bayesian inference problems. The generator is constructed using a U-Net architecture, with the latent information injected using conditional instance normalization. The former facilitates a multiscale inverse map, while the latter enables the decoupling of the latent space dimension from the dimension of the measurement, and introduces stochasticity at all scales of the U-Net.

arxiv-2205-00177.title: Practice Makes a Solver Perfect: Data Augmentation for Math Word Problem Solvers
arxiv-2205-00177.creator: Vivek Kumar, Rishabh Maheshwary, Vikram Pudi
arxiv-2205-00177.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vivek Kumar, Rishabh Maheshwary, Vikram Pudi. Existing Math Word Problem (MWP) solvers have achieved high accuracy on benchmark datasets. However, prior works have shown that such solvers do not generalize well and rely on superficial cues to achieve high performance. In this paper, we first conduct experiments to showcase that this behaviour is mainly associated with the limited size and diversity present in existing MWP datasets. Next, we propose several data augmentation techniques broadly categorized into Substitution and Paraphrasing based methods.

arxiv-2304-14796.creator: Sonal Sannigrahi, Josef van Genabith, Cristina España-Bonet
arxiv-2304-14796.description: Abstract Dense vector representations for textual data are crucial in modern NLP. arxiv-2312-17363.creator: Dandan Tang and Xin Tong
arxiv-2312-17363.description: Abstract Missing data are inevitable in longitudinal studies. Traditional methods, such as the full information maximum likelihood (FIML), are commonly used to handle ignorable missing data. However, they may lead to biased model estimation due to missing not at random data that often appear in longitudinal studies.

arxiv-2403-14363.title: Multi-player quantum data hiding by nonlocal quantum state ensembles
arxiv-2403-14363.creator: Donghoon Ha, Jeong San Kim
arxiv-2403-14363.description: Abstract We provide multi-player quantum data hiding based on nonlocal quantum state ensembles arising from multi-party quantum state discrimination. Using bounds on local minimum-error discrimination of multi-party quantum states, we construct a multi-player quantum data-hiding scheme. Our data-hiding scheme can be used to hide multiple bits, asymptotically, unless all the players collaborate.

Another area of interest are vector-like quarks which lie at the heart of many extensions to the Standard Model seeking to address the Hierarchy Problem, as they can naturally cancel the mass divergence for the Higgs boson.
